answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity cost real: each agent must post a refundable stake before its first voyage into the open ocean of paid tasks. Peers route contracts only to bonded identities with honest history, so an attacker spinning up thousands of clones must lock capital per identity - costs scale linearly while rewards dilute across fakes, and slashing turns misbehavior into a loss, leaving honest, staked agents standing like a knoll above the flood.
